stories.summary: Cocaine-funded militias are attacking civilians in Colombia eight years after a peace agreement removed a major rebel group from the conflict. The Wall Street Journal report attributes the renewed insecurity to state inaction that allowed powerful armed groups to operate in the vacuum.

links.headline: Cocaine-Funded Gangs Shake Colombia Years After Peace Pact
links.excerpt: Attacks by powerful militias against civilians reflect the state’s inaction eight years after a peace accord removed a powerful rebel group from the field.

stories.title: Canada Is Becoming a Fentanyl Exporter, and a Target for Trump
stories.summary: Fentanyl is increasingly being manufactured in and trafficked from Canada, drawing scrutiny from President Donald Trump. The quantities remain small compared with those associated with Mexico, according to the Wall Street Journal report.

links.headline: Canada Is Becoming a Fentanyl Exporter, and a Target for Trump
links.excerpt: The drug is increasingly manufactured in and trafficked from the U.S.’s northern neighbor, though the numbers remain small compared with Mexico.
